To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the energy return on investment (EROFIs) for ultra-deep-water oil and gas in the GoM in 2009 were low (i.e., less than a gallon of energy per dollar invested), and (2) the energy return of the oil reserves of the Deepwater Horizon (Macondo Prospect) oil spill in the GoM were even lower (i.e., about a half gallon of energy per barrel).
the EROI of ultra-deep oil in the GoM in 2009 ranged from 7 to 22:1, and the EROI of the Maconda oil reserve ranged from 4 to 16:1.

the energy return on investment for the ultra-deep water oil and natural gas production of the GoM in 2009 ranged from 0 to 22:1, and that the energy return of the Maconda Prospect oil reserves was 4 to 16:1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the economic and energetic costs of ultra-depewater energy production.
the energetic and economic cost-benefit of ultra-deep-water drilling in the GoM.
the energy and financial costs of extracting oil and gas in the ultra-depwater GoM, and the energy return on investment for the Macondo oil reserves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ultra-deepwater production is a net energy loser for the United States.
ultra-deepwater GoM oil and gas production is not an efficient use of energy and financial resources.
the EROFI of ultra-deep-water oil and gas is very low and EROI is low to moderate, and both measures of energy efficiency are likely to decrease in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy and economic costs of oil extraction in the ultra-deeepwater of the Gulf of Mexico are increasing, and that the EROI of the oil reserves at Macondo Prospect are low.
ultra-deepwater drilling in the GoM has a low EROI and EROFI, and that these energy and financial costs are increasing.
ultra-deepwater GoM oil and gas production is an expensive proposition for society and the EROI of the Macondowellhead reserves is in the range of 4 to 16:1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ultra-deep-water GoM oil and natural gas reserves have an energy return to society that is lower than the energy invested in producing these energy resources.
the EROFI and EROI of ultra-deep water oil and natural gas in the GoM are very low.
the ultra-deep water GoM oil and gas is an energy intensive endeavor.
